title: Strict (distinct-variable) two-color Rado numbers for x+y=kz
domain: Ramsey theory / Rado numbers (combinatorial number theory)
problem: Determine RR*_2(k) = min N such that every 2-coloring of [N] has a monochromatic pairwise-distinct solution to x+y=kz, for all k.
hypothesis: RR*_2(k) = (k^2+2k+2)/2 for even k>=8; (k^2+3k)/2 for odd k>=9; sporadic values 9,15,20,25,31,49 at k=2..7.
baseline: Non-strict family classical: A100542, Burr-Loo, Harborth-Maasberg 1999, Jones-Schaal 2004.
proposed_improvement: Full determination of the distinct-variable family incl. formula and exceptions.

experimental_evidence.what: exact RR*_2(k) for k=1..30 by two independent solvers (DFS + CaDiCaL SAT), validated on S(2)=5, S(3)=14
experimental_evidence.how_to_reproduce: python research/sessions/S6/code/sat_solver.py rado 30 2 weak ; python research/sessions/S6/code/solver.py interval 30 2 weak
experimental_evidence.result: formula matches all k in [8,30]; table archived in experiments/S6/

adversarial_attacks.attack: literature novelty audit (50 tool calls: arXiv API, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, OEIS)
adversarial_attacks.outcome: DIRECT PRIOR ART: A. Towell, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19372727 (2026-04-01) + OEIS A394445 (approved 2026-03): same table to k=500, same parity-split closed form, same exceptions, complete claimed proof.

novelty_notes: Identical theorem published April 2026 (Towell). Our computation is an independent confirmation; no first-determination claim possible. See sessions/S6/postmortems/C-001.md.
next_action: Pivot to cyclic variant C-S6-002: 2-colorings of Z_n avoiding mono distinct x+y=kz (mod n); classification unknown as of interim search.
